items.stem: Which practice correctly mitigates reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) in PHP output?

options.text: Escaping user-derived data for the HTML context before output
options.rationale: Context-appropriate output escaping neutralises injected markup/script.

options.text: Storing the data in a session
options.rationale: Sessions do not neutralise XSS in output.
Comparison operators are unrelated to XSS.
Compression has no bearing on XSS.

items.explanation: Context-appropriate output escaping neutralises injected markup/script.

items.stem: Select TWO benefits of using a generator with yield for large datasets in PHP.

options.text: Values are produced lazily, keeping memory use low
options.rationale: Generators yield one item at a time instead of building a full array.

options.text: It can represent an effectively unbounded sequence
options.rationale: Generators can stream without materialising everything.

options.text: It guarantees the data is sorted
It loads the entire dataset into memory first
options.rationale: That is the opposite of a generator's purpose.

items.explanation: Generators yield one item at a time instead of building a full array.

items.stem: Why inject dependencies rather than instantiate them inside a class?

options.text: It decouples the class from concrete implementations and eases testing
options.rationale: Injection lets you substitute implementations and mocks, improving testability.

options.text: It makes the class run without any dependencies
options.rationale: The dependencies still exist; only their wiring changes.

options.text: It removes the need for interfaces

options.rationale: Injection is about wiring, not caching.

items.explanation: Injection lets you substitute implementations and mocks, improving testability.
